title: How Alice Huang-Linked Firms Used AI Servers to Secure Financing in China
text:
Daniel Nenni
Founder
Staff member

Companies connected to the family and business associates of Alice Huang used AI computing equipment to secure financing in China, according to central-bank credit records reviewed by Reuters. The filings list up to 764 servers and computing modules valued at $270 million, plus $31 million in networking equipment. The figures represent declared asset values in financing records and may include overlapping listings.

Century Litong, a server rental company, arranged five leases from May through December 2024 covering up to 512 servers valued at roughly $200 million. Four filings identified Shanghai’s Yangtze River Delta AI supercomputing center as an equipment location. In a separate deal, Wuhu Century Longteng pledged 252 computing modules to Ping An Bank as collateral for a $70 million loan in April 2026. Reuters traced corporate ties to Huang’s sister and husband through company records.

The report comes as U.S. authorities investigate whether Megaspeed, a Singapore-based company Huang formerly controlled, helped Chinese customers obtain restricted Nvidia technology. The U.S. Commerce Department added Megaspeed to its trade blacklist on November 23. Megaspeed denied wrongdoing and said Huang left the company in August 2025. The filings leave open which processors were inside the servers and when or how the equipment entered China.

Equipment leases and collateral pledges show how operators can finance the large upfront cost of building AI infrastructure. Leasing lets a company spread payments over time, while pledging hardware lets it borrow against assets it already holds. The financing records also offer a view into the infrastructure beyond the processors themselves. Networking equipment connects individual servers so they can work together on computing jobs too large for a single machine. A credit registry can therefore reveal the scale and location of a computing project while leaving the origin of its chips unresolved.
